statement: A rectangular raised garden bed is $6$ feet long and $3.5$ feet wide. It will be filled with soil to a depth of $1.5$ feet. Soil is sold in bags that each hold $2$ cubic feet. What is the least number of bags needed to fill the bed to that depth?

choices.misconception: I added the three dimensions to get $11$ instead of multiplying them, then divided by 2 and rounded up to 6.
I used only the area of the top, $6 \times 3.5 = 21$ square feet, and ignored the depth, so $21 \div 2 = 10.5$ rounded up to 11.
I found $31.5 \div 2 = 15.75$ bags and rounded down to 15, but 15 bags leave the bed short of soil.

hints: Find how much space the soil fills.
The volume of a rectangular box is length times width times depth. Then see how many 2-cubic-foot bags that takes.
The volume is $6 \times 3.5 \times 1.5 = 31.5$ cubic feet, and $31.5 \div 2 = 15.75$. You cannot buy part of a bag.

solutions.reliable: The soil fills a rectangular prism, so its volume is $6 \times 3.5 \times 1.5 = 31.5$ cubic feet. Each bag holds $2$ cubic feet, so $31.5 \div 2 = 15.75$ bags are needed. Fifteen bags hold only $30$ cubic feet, which is not enough, so the least number is $16$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
